title.en: From the Hundred-Plant Garden to the Three-Flavour Study

edition.en: Transcribed by Claude from a scan of a 1941 reprint of Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk (朝花夕拾; Lu Xun Thirty Years Collection, vol. 16) on Wikimedia Commons, and checked against the Wikisource text; written 18 September 1926, first published in Mangyuan (莽原) in October 1926, and collected in Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk, 1928.
edition.zh: 据维基共享资源所藏《朝花夕拾》1941 年重印本（《鲁迅三十年集》第十六册）扫描页，由 Claude 校录，并与维基文库本对校；作于 1926 年 9 月 18 日，同年 10 月初刊于《莽原》，1928 年收入《朝花夕拾》。

basis.en: First published in 1926; the author died in 1936. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1926 年首次发表，作者卒于 1936 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: Lu Xun’s memory of the overgrown garden behind his family’s house, with its crickets, raspberries and snow traps, and of the strict old school where his teacher would not tell him about the insect called Strange-Indeed. It is here because few pieces show so clearly two ways a child learns: from a garden that answers everything, and from a teacher who answers nothing. Notice the ‘Ade’ (German for goodbye) that he gives to his crickets.
note.zh: 鲁迅回忆家后那座荒园里的蟋蟀、覆盆子和雪地捕鸟，以及那所严厉的书塾，先生不肯告诉他“怪哉”这种虫是怎么一回事。收在这里，是因为很少有文章把孩子学习的两条路写得这样清楚：一座什么都回答的园子，和一位什么都不回答的先生。留意他对蟋蟀们说的那声“Ade”（德语的“再见”）。

excerpt.orig: Ade，我的蟋蟀們！Ade，我的覆盆子們和木蓮們！
excerpt.en: Ade, my crickets! Ade, my raspberries and climbing figs!
excerpt.zh: Ade，我的蟋蟀们！Ade，我的覆盆子们和木莲们！

gloss.en: Zhu Wengong is Zhu Xi (1130–1200), the great Confucian philosopher, honoured after death with the name Wen. The family that bought the house in 1919 was surnamed Zhu; calling them his descendants is Lu Xun’s irony.
gloss.zh: 朱文公：南宋理学家朱熹（1130–1200），谥号“文”。1919 年买下周家房子的人家姓朱，说他们是朱文公的子孙，是鲁迅的讽刺。

gloss.en: 何首烏: fleeceflower, a medicinal vine with tuberous roots. The name means ‘Mr He’s black hair’, from a story of an old man whose white hair turned black again after he ate the root.
gloss.zh: 何首乌：多年生藤本植物，块根可入药。相传有姓何的老人吃了它，白发变黑，因而得名。

gloss.en: Mother Chang: Ah Chang, the nurse who looked after Lu Xun as a boy. He wrote about her in ‘Ah Chang and the Classic of Mountains and Seas’, in the same book as this essay.
gloss.zh: 长妈妈：即阿长，鲁迅幼年的保姆。《朝花夕拾》中另有《阿长与〈山海经〉》写她。

gloss.en: Zhang Fei: the fierce, hot-tempered general of the Three Kingdoms, here lending his name to a small bird with a temper.
gloss.zh: 张飞：三国时蜀汉的猛将，性情暴躁，这种鸟因脾气躁而得名。

gloss.en: Ade: German for ‘goodbye’, from the French adieu. Lu Xun had learned German in Japan.
gloss.zh: Ade：德语，“再见”的意思（源自法语 adieu）。鲁迅在日本留学时学过德语。

gloss.en: The Three-Flavour Study: a private school run by Shou Jingwu (1849–1930). The three flavours are usually explained as the classics, the histories and the philosophers, which taste like grain, meat and sauce.
gloss.zh: 三味书屋：寿镜吾（1849–1930）开设的私塾。“三味”一般解作：读经味如稻粱，读史味如肴馔，读诸子百家味如醯醢。

gloss.en: A deer is a lucky picture: 鹿 (lù) sounds like 祿, an official’s emolument, so it wishes the pupils success.
gloss.zh: 梅花鹿：“鹿”谐音“禄”，寓意功名利禄，是吉祥画。

gloss.en: Dongfang Shuo (2nd–1st century BCE): the witty, learned courtier of the Han emperor Wu. In the old story, the ‘Strange-Indeed’ insect was born from the grief of people wrongly imprisoned under Qin, and dissolved in wine, because wine dispels sorrow.
gloss.zh: 东方朔：西汉武帝时以博学诙谐著称的文人。相传“怪哉”虫是秦时冤狱中百姓的怨气所化，用酒浇它便消散，因为酒能解忧。

gloss.en: 對課: an exercise in parallel phrasing. The teacher gives a phrase and the pupil answers it with one that matches word for word in sense and tone, the training for writing verse.
gloss.zh: 对课：老师出上联，学生对下联，字数、词性、平仄都要相对，是学作诗文的基本训练。

gloss.at: 仁遠乎哉我欲仁斯仁至矣
gloss.at_hans: 仁远乎哉我欲仁斯仁至矣
gloss.en: The boys are reading different books at once: the Analects (7.30), the primer Youxue qionglin, the Book of Changes and the ‘Tribute of Yu’ in the Book of Documents. The Changes actually has 初九, not 上九, for the hidden dragon, and the Documents line is pieced together from several sentences.
gloss.zh: 孩子们各读各的书：“仁远乎哉”出自《论语·述而》，“笑人齿缺”出自《幼学琼林》，“潜龙勿用”出自《周易·乾卦》，“厥土下上上错”出自《尚书·禹贡》。《周易》原文是“初九”，不是“上九”；《禹贡》的那一句也是几处文字拼合起来的。

gloss.en: From a rhapsody by the Qing writer Liu Han on the late Tang general Li Keyong holding a feast at Sanchui Hill: the teacher’s favourite passage.
gloss.zh: 出自清代刘翰的《李克用置酒三垂冈赋》。李克用是唐末的将领。

gloss.en: 錫箔: paper coated with tin, folded into the shape of ingots and burned as offerings to ancestors and gods; Shaoxing was famous for making it.
gloss.zh: 锡箔：涂上锡的纸，折成元宝形状，祭祀时焚化。绍兴以出产锡箔著称。

note.en: A garden that answers everything and a teacher who answers nothing, set side by side without comment; among the best of Lu Xun’s memoirs, light-handed and exact.
note.zh: 什么都回答的园子，什么都不回答的先生，并置而不加评论；鲁迅回忆文字中的佳作，笔轻而准。
